passages.text: “Son of man,” He said to me, “eat what you find here. Eat this scroll, then go and speak to the house of Israel.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to me.
He called me "son of man."
God told me to eat what I found in front of me.
He told me to eat the scroll.
God commanded me to go.
He told me to speak to the house of Israel.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י בֶּן־ אָדָ֕ם אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־ תִּמְצָ֖א אֱכ֑וֹל אֱכוֹל֙ אֶת־ הַמְּגִלָּ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את וְלֵ֥ךְ דַּבֵּ֖ר אֶל־ בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: So I opened my mouth, and He fed me the scroll.
passages.sermon:
Ezekiel was a prophet.
God spoke to Ezekiel.
God gave Ezekiel a vision.
I opened my mouth.
God gave me the scroll to eat.
God fed me the scroll.
passages.original: וָאֶפְתַּ֖ח אֶת־ פִּ֑י וַיַּ֣אֲכִלֵ֔נִי אֵ֖ת הַמְּגִלָּ֥ה הַזֹּֽאת׃

passages.text: “Son of man,” He said to me, “eat and fill your stomach with this scroll I am giving you.” So I ate, and it was as sweet as honey in my mouth.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to me.
He called me “son of man.”
God told me to eat the scroll He was giving me.
He told me to fill my stomach with it.
I ate the scroll.
The scroll tasted as sweet as honey in my mouth.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י בֶּן־ אָדָם֙ בִּטְנְךָ֤ תַֽאֲכֵל֙ וּמֵעֶ֣יךָ תְמַלֵּ֔א אֵ֚ת הַמְּגִלָּ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲנִ֖י נֹתֵ֣ן אֵלֶ֑יךָ וָאֹ֣כְלָ֔ה וַתְּהִ֥י בְּפִ֖י כִּדְבַ֥שׁ לְמָתֽוֹק׃פ

passages.text: Then He said to me, “Son of man, go now to the house of Israel and speak My words to them.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to me.
He called me "son of man."
He told me to go to the house of Israel.
He commanded me to speak His words to them.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֵלָ֑י בֶּן־ אָדָ֗ם לֶךְ־ בֹּא֙ אֶל־ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְדִבַּרְתָּ֥ בִדְבָרַ֖י אֲלֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: For you are not being sent to a people of unfamiliar speech or difficult language, but to the house of Israel— not to the many peoples of unfamiliar speech and difficult language whose words you cannot understand. Surely if I had sent you to them, they would have listened to you.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel.
God called Ezekiel “son of man.”
God sent Ezekiel to the house of Israel.
God did not send Ezekiel to a people with a strange language.
God did not send Ezekiel to a people with difficult speech.
God did not send Ezekiel to many nations with unfamiliar speech.
God did not send Ezekiel to people whose words he could not understand.
If God had sent Ezekiel to those foreign nations, they would have listened to him.
passages.original: כִּ֡י לֹא֩ אֶל־ עַ֨ם עִמְקֵ֥י שָׂפָ֛ה וְכִבְדֵ֥י לָשׁ֖וֹן אַתָּ֣ה שָׁל֑וּחַ אֶל־ בֵּ֖ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ לֹ֣א׀ אֶל־ עַמִּ֣ים רַבִּ֗ים עִמְקֵ֤י שָׂפָה֙ וְכִבְדֵ֣י לָשׁ֔וֹן אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־ תִשְׁמַ֖ע דִּבְרֵיהֶ֑ם אִם־ לֹ֤א אֲלֵיהֶם֙ שְׁלַחְתִּ֔יךָ הֵ֖מָּה יִשְׁמְע֥וּ אֵלֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: But the house of Israel will be unwilling to listen to you, since they are unwilling to listen to Me. For the whole house of Israel is hard-headed and hard-hearted.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel.
God called Ezekiel “son of man.”
God sent Ezekiel to the house of Israel.
The house of Israel will not listen to you.
They do not want to listen to you.
They do not want to listen to Me.
All the people of Israel are stubborn.
They are hard-headed.
They are hard-hearted.
passages.original: וּבֵ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לֹ֤א יֹאבוּ֙ לִשְׁמֹ֣עַ אֵלֶ֔יךָ כִּֽי־ אֵינָ֥ם אֹבִ֖ים לִשְׁמֹ֣עַ אֵלָ֑י כִּ֚י כָּל־ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל חִזְקֵי־ מֵ֥צַח וּקְשֵׁי־ לֵ֖ב הֵֽמָּה׃

passages.text: Behold, I will make your face as hard as their faces, and your forehead as hard as their foreheads.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel.
God sent Ezekiel to the house of Israel.
The people of Israel are stubborn and rebellious.
God said, “I will make your face strong like their faces.
I will make your forehead hard like their foreheads.”
passages.original: הִנֵּ֨ה נָתַ֧תִּי אֶת־ פָּנֶ֛יךָ חֲזָקִ֖ים לְעֻמַּ֣ת פְּנֵיהֶ֑ם וְאֶֽת־ מִצְחֲךָ֥ חָזָ֖ק לְעֻמַּ֥ת מִצְחָֽם׃

passages.text: I will make your forehead like a diamond, harder than flint. Do not be afraid of them or dismayed at their presence, even though they are a rebellious house.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel.
God said, “I will make your forehead very hard.
Your forehead will be like a diamond.
Your forehead will be harder than flint.
Do not be afraid of the people of Israel.
Do not be discouraged when you see them.
The people of Israel are a rebellious house.”
passages.original: כְּשָׁמִ֛יר חָזָ֥ק מִצֹּ֖ר נָתַ֣תִּי מִצְחֶ֑ךָ לֹֽא־ תִירָ֤א אוֹתָם֙ וְלֹא־ תֵחַ֣ת מִפְּנֵיהֶ֔ם כִּ֛י בֵּֽית־ מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה׃פ

passages.text: “Son of man,” He added, “listen carefully to all the words I speak to you, and take them to heart.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel.
God called Ezekiel "son of man."
God told Ezekiel to listen to His words.
God told Ezekiel to hear every word with his ears.
God told Ezekiel to keep all His words in his heart.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֵלָ֑י בֶּן־ אָדָ֕ם אֶת־ כָּל־ דְּבָרַי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֲדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלֶ֔יךָ קַ֥ח בִּֽלְבָבְךָ֖ וּבְאָזְנֶ֥יךָ שְׁמָֽע׃

passages.text: Go to your people, the exiles; speak to them and tell them, ‘This is what the Lord GOD says,’ whether they listen or refuse to listen.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel.
Ezekiel was a prophet.
God told Ezekiel to go to the exiles.
The exiles were Ezekiel’s own people.
God commanded Ezekiel to speak to them.
God told Ezekiel to say, “This is what the Lord GOD says.”
God said to speak these words whether the people listen or not.
God said to speak even if the people refuse to listen.
passages.original: וְלֵ֨ךְ בֹּ֤א אֶל־ הַגּוֹלָה֙ אֶל־ בְּנֵ֣י עַמֶּ֔ךָ וְדִבַּרְתָּ֤ אֲלֵיהֶם֙ וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֑ה אִֽם־ יִשְׁמְע֖וּ וְאִם־ יֶחְדָּֽלוּ׃

passages.text: Then the Spirit lifted me up, and I heard a great rumbling sound behind me: ‘Blessed be the glory of the LORD in His dwelling place!’
passages.sermon: The Spirit lifted me up.\r\nI heard a great rumbling sound behind me.\r\nPeople said, “Blessed be the glory of the LORD in His dwelling place!”
passages.original: וַתִּשָּׂאֵ֣נִי ר֔וּחַ וָאֶשְׁמַ֣ע אַחֲרַ֔י ק֖וֹל רַ֣עַשׁ גָּד֑וֹל בָּר֥וּךְ כְּבוֹד־ יְהוָ֖ה מִמְּקוֹמֽוֹ׃

passages.text: It was the sound of the wings of the living creatures brushing against one another and the sound of the wheels beside them, a great rumbling sound.
passages.sermon:
The living creatures had wings.
Their wings touched each other.
The wings made a sound as they brushed together.
Wheels stood beside the living creatures.
The wheels made a sound.
There was a great rumbling sound.
passages.original: וְק֣וֹל׀ כַּנְפֵ֣י הַחַיּ֗וֹת מַשִּׁיקוֹת֙ אִשָּׁ֣ה אֶל־ אֲחוֹתָ֔הּ וְק֥וֹל הָאוֹפַנִּ֖ים לְעֻמָּתָ֑ם וְק֖וֹל רַ֥עַשׁ גָּדֽוֹל׃

passages.text: So the Spirit lifted me up and took me away, and I went in bitterness and in the anger of my spirit, with the strong hand of the LORD upon me.
passages.sermon:
The Spirit of God lifted me up.
The Spirit took me away.
I went in bitterness.
I went with anger in my spirit.
The strong hand of the LORD was upon me.
passages.original: וְר֥וּחַ נְשָׂאַ֖תְנִי וַתִּקָּחֵ֑נִי וָאֵלֵ֥ךְ מַר֙ בַּחֲמַ֣ת רוּחִ֔י וְיַד־ יְהוָ֥ה עָלַ֖י חָזָֽקָה׃

passages.text: I came to the exiles at Tel-abib who dwelt by the River Kebar. And for seven days I sat where they sat and remained there among them, overwhelmed.
passages.sermon:
Ezekiel was a prophet of God.
He came to the exiles at Tel-abib.
These exiles lived by the River Kebar.
Ezekiel went to where they lived.
He sat there with them for seven days.
He stayed among them.
He was overwhelmed as he sat with them.
passages.original: וָאָב֨וֹא אֶל־ הַגּוֹלָ֜ה תֵּ֣ל אָ֠בִיב הַיֹּשְׁבִ֤ים אֶֽל־ נְהַר־ כְּבָר֙ וָאֲשֶׁר הֵ֖מָּה יוֹשְׁבִ֣ים שָׁ֑ם וָאֵשֵׁ֥ב שָׁ֛ם שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים מַשְׁמִ֥ים בְּתוֹכָֽם׃

passages.text: At the end of seven days the word of the LORD came to me, saying, “Son of man, I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel. Whenever you hear a word from My mouth, give them a warning from Me.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to me after seven days.
He gave me a message.
He called me “son of man.”
He said, “I have made you a watchman.”
He made me a watchman for the house of Israel.
He told me to listen to His words.
He said, “When you hear a word from Me, warn the people for Me.”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֕י מִקְצֵ֖ה שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֑ים פ וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־ יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃ בֶּן־ אָדָ֕ם צֹפֶ֥ה נְתַתִּ֖יךָ לְבֵ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְשָׁמַעְתָּ֤ מִפִּי֙ דָּבָ֔ר וְהִזְהַרְתָּ֥ אוֹתָ֖ם מִמֶּֽנִּי׃

passages.text: If I say to the wicked man, ‘You will surely die,’ but you do not warn him or speak out to warn him from his wicked way to save his life, that wicked man will die in his iniquity, and I will hold you responsible for his blood.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Ezekiel.
God says, “If I tell a wicked man, ‘You will surely die,’ this is a warning.
You, Ezekiel, must warn the wicked man.
You must speak to warn him to turn from his wicked way.
You must try to save his life.
If you do not warn the wicked man,
If you do not speak to warn him to turn from his evil way,
That wicked man will die because of his sin.
I, God, will hold you responsible for his blood.”
passages.original: בְּאָמְרִ֤י לָֽרָשָׁע֙ מ֣וֹת תָּמ֔וּת וְלֹ֣א הִזְהַרְתּ֗וֹ וְלֹ֥א דִבַּ֛רְתָּ לְהַזְהִ֥יר רָשָׁ֛ע מִדַּרְכּ֥וֹ הָרְשָׁעָ֖ה לְחַיֹּת֑וֹ ה֤וּא רָשָׁע֙ בַּעֲוֺנ֣וֹ יָמ֔וּת וְדָמ֖וֹ מִיָּדְךָ֥ אֲבַקֵּֽשׁ׃

passages.text: But if you warn a wicked man and he does not turn from his wickedness and his wicked way, he will die in his iniquity, but you will have saved yourself.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel.
God made Ezekiel a watchman for Israel.
God gave Ezekiel a duty to warn people.
If you warn a wicked man, you have done your duty.
If the wicked man does not turn from his wickedness, he will not change his evil way.
That wicked man will die because of his sin.
You will save yourself because you warned him.
passages.original: וְאַתָּה֙ כִּֽי־ הִזְהַ֣רְתָּ רָשָׁ֔ע וְלֹא־ שָׁב֙ מֵֽרִשְׁע֔וֹ וּמִדַּרְכּ֖וֹ הָרְשָׁעָ֑ה ה֚וּא בַּעֲוֺנ֣וֹ יָמ֔וּת וְאַתָּ֖ה אֶֽת־ נַפְשְׁךָ֥ הִצַּֽלְתָּ׃ס

passages.text: Now if a righteous man turns from his righteousness and commits iniquity, and I put a stumbling block before him, he will die. If you did not warn him, he will die in his sin, and the righteous acts he did will not be remembered. And I will hold you responsible for his blood.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel the prophet.
God gave Ezekiel a warning about righteous people.
A righteous man lives in a way that pleases God.
Sometimes a righteous man turns away from his righteousness.
He chooses to do what is wrong.
God may put a stumbling block in front of him.
This man will die because of his sin.
If you, Ezekiel, do not warn this man,
he will die in his sin.
God will not remember the good things he did before.
God will hold you, Ezekiel, responsible for his death.
passages.original: וּבְשׁ֨וּב צַדִּ֤יק מִצִּדְקוֹ֙ וְעָ֣שָׂה עָ֔וֶל וְנָתַתִּ֥י מִכְשׁ֛וֹל לְפָנָ֖יו ה֣וּא יָמ֑וּת כִּ֣י לֹ֤א הִזְהַרְתּוֹ֙ בְּחַטָּאת֣וֹ יָמ֔וּת וְלֹ֣א תִזָּכַ֗רְןָ צִדְקֹתָו֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה וְדָמ֖וֹ מִיָּדְךָ֥ אֲבַקֵּֽשׁ׃

passages.text: But if you warn the righteous man not to sin, and he does not sin, he will indeed live because he heeded your warning, and you will have saved yourself.”
passages.sermon:
You warn a righteous man not to sin.
The righteous man does not sin.
He lives.
He lives because he listened to your warning.
You save yourself.
passages.original: וְאַתָּ֞ה כִּ֧י הִזְהַרְתּ֣וֹ צַדִּ֗יק לְבִלְתִּ֥י חֲטֹ֛א צַדִּ֖יק וְה֣וּא לֹא־ חָטָ֑א חָי֤וֹ יִֽחְיֶה֙ כִּ֣י נִזְהָ֔ר וְאַתָּ֖ה אֶֽת־ נַפְשְׁךָ֥ הִצַּֽלְתָּ׃ס

passages.text: And there the hand of the LORD was upon me, and He said to me, “Get up, go out to the plain, and there I will speak with you.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD put His hand on me.
He spoke to me.
He said, "Get up."
He said, "Go out to the plain."
He said, "There I will speak with you."
passages.original: וַתְּהִ֥י עָלַ֛י שָׁ֖ם יַד־ יְהוָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י ק֥וּם צֵא֙ אֶל־ הַבִּקְעָ֔ה וְשָׁ֖ם אֲדַבֵּ֥ר אוֹתָֽךְ׃

passages.text: So I got up and went out to the plain, and behold, the glory of the LORD was present there, like the glory I had seen by the River Kebar, and I fell facedown.
passages.sermon:
Ezekiel was a prophet.
God spoke to Ezekiel.
God told Ezekiel to get up.
God told Ezekiel to go out to the plain.
I got up.
I went out to the plain.
I saw the glory of the LORD there.
The glory of the LORD stood before me.
This glory looked like the glory I saw by the River Kebar.
I fell facedown.
passages.original: וָאָקוּם֮ וָאֵצֵ֣א אֶל־ הַבִּקְעָה֒ וְהִנֵּה־ שָׁ֤ם כְּבוֹד־ יְהוָה֙ עֹמֵ֔ד כַּכָּב֕וֹד אֲשֶׁ֥ר רָאִ֖יתִי עַל־ נְהַר־ כְּבָ֑ר וָאֶפֹּ֖ל עַל־ פָּנָֽי׃

passages.text: Then the Spirit entered me and set me on my feet. He spoke with me and said, “Go, shut yourself inside your house.
passages.sermon:
The Spirit of the LORD entered me.
The Spirit set me on my feet.
The LORD spoke to me.
He said to me, "Go inside your house."
He said, "Shut yourself inside your house."
passages.original: וַתָּבֹא־ בִ֣י ר֔וּחַ וַתַּעֲמִדֵ֖נִי עַל־ רַגְלָ֑י וַיְדַבֵּ֤ר אֹתִי֙ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י בֹּ֥א הִסָּגֵ֖ר בְּת֥וֹךְ בֵּיתֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: And you, son of man, they will tie with ropes, and you will be bound so that you cannot go out among the people.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel.
Ezekiel was a prophet.
God called Ezekiel "son of man."
People will tie ropes around you, Ezekiel.
They will bind you with these ropes.
You will not be able to go out among the people.
passages.original: וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן־ אָדָ֗ם הִנֵּ֨ה נָתְנ֤וּ עָלֶ֙יךָ֙ עֲבוֹתִ֔ים וַאֲסָר֖וּךָ בָּהֶ֑ם וְלֹ֥א תֵצֵ֖א בְּתוֹכָֽם׃

passages.text: I will make your tongue stick to the roof of your mouth, and you will be silent and unable to rebuke them, though they are a rebellious house.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel, the son of man.
God said, “I will make your tongue stick to the roof of your mouth.”
You will become silent.
You will not be able to rebuke the people.
The people are a rebellious house.
passages.original: וּלְשֽׁוֹנְךָ֙ אַדְבִּ֣יק אֶל־ חִכֶּ֔ךָ וְנֶֽאֱלַ֔מְתָּ וְלֹא־ תִֽהְיֶ֥ה לָהֶ֖ם לְאִ֣ישׁ מוֹכִ֑יחַ כִּ֛י בֵּ֥ית מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה׃

passages.text: But when I speak with you, I will open your mouth, and you are to tell them, ‘This is what the Lord GOD says.’ Whoever listens, let him listen; and whoever refuses, let him refuse, for they are a rebellious house.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel, the son of man.
God said, “When I speak with you, I will open your mouth.”
You will speak to the people.
You will say to them, ‘This is what the Lord GOD says.’
Some people will listen.
Let those who listen, listen.
Some people will refuse.
Let those who refuse, refuse.
They are a rebellious house.
passages.original: וּֽבְדַבְּרִ֤י אֽוֹתְךָ֙ אֶפְתַּ֣ח אֶת־ פִּ֔יךָ וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֑ה הַשֹּׁמֵ֤עַ׀ יִשְׁמָע֙ וְהֶחָדֵ֣ל׀ יֶחְדָּ֔ל כִּ֛י בֵּ֥ית מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה׃ס
